key_insight: A single randomly Pauli-dressed circuit can suppress coherent error accumulation when correlations between transported error generators would otherwise amplify it.
engineering_relevance: For structured quantum circuits, Pauli dressing can improve fidelity without averaging over multiple randomized circuit compilations.
method: Relate leading infidelity under weak coherent errors to accumulated error-generator variance.
Independently Pauli-dress two-qubit Clifford gates to remove cross-layer contributions on average.
Use a covariance diagnostic to predict when dressing is beneficial.
evidence_signal: Theory and simulations show possible quadratic variance growth in bare circuits versus a linear bound at fixed confidence for one random dressed realization; IBM hardware experiments demonstrate improved GHZ fidelity and reduced observable errors in Trotterized transverse-field Ising dynamics.
watch_item: The analysis assumes weak coherent errors, and little benefit is expected when the transported-generator covariance matrix is nearly diagonal.
paper_title: Single-realization Pauli twirling for suppressing coherent error accumulation in structured quantum circuits
